DAL are soft against the run (133 yds/game allowed), and HOU feed Woody Marks a heavy 58% carry share — a rushing-yards spot.

The HOU host the DAL as favorites of 2.5, with the total set at 47.5 — a market that implies a HOU 25–22 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with HOU in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with HOU chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 2.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for Javonte Williams — HOU are stingy against the run (100 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

C.J. Stroud has a passing-yards tailwind — DAL allow 252 pass yds/game (vs ~230).

Sneaky value on Xavier Hutchinson (WR2) — DAL leak 43 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Touchdown Board

Jake Ferguson is a live anytime-TD dart — HOU are leaky to tight ends in the end zone (0.34 TE TDs/game vs ~0.24).

Nico Collins carries TD equity — DAL surrender 0.59 WR1 receiving scores a game.

In the red zone DAL throw it (58% pass inside the 20) — George Pickens's TD equity over a goal-line back.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

A middling 48 total — no strong lean either way; the value is in the individual matchups above, not the game environment.

Both teams play at a quick tempo (~64 plays each) — extra snaps lift everyone's counting stats.

HOU — a balanced offense

HOU are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (43% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Woody Marks (13 carries, 48 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Nico Collins projects for 6 targets and 57 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Dalton Schultz (TE, 4 targets, 30 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 2-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.
